actions.reason: b58decode_int now takes ten digits per big-integer step, where it used to take five. Each group of ten is read as two five-digit small ints (hi, lo). They are combined as hi * base**5 + lo and folded into the accumulator with one multiply-add by base**10. This halves the number of big-integer multiply-adds, slices and unpacks per decoded string. The leading n % 10 digits are still folded one digit at a time, so the result is the same integer. Outputs match the parent exactly (equivalence harness). Measured ratios: decode_ir 0.9432, check_ir 0.9847, encode_ir 1.0010 (unchanged code path).
